_: The dock the clip films, as a table. `mode` is not a claim about a row:
it picks which script bin/agent.sh runs, and the badge is whatever the
orchestrator makes of that script's output. `run` is how many seconds
after W (the moment every agent starts together) the row stops talking;
its badge lands `run` + IDLE_AFTER_MS (5s) later, which is what staggers
the six checks on camera -- 0.6s apart, which is as tight as the default
5s idle window allows without moving the whole cascade later.
A `done` run under ~2.0 does not work: coding_agent.py waits 0.5s before
its first line, so the burst is `run` - 0.5, and it has to clear
WORK_MIN_MS (1.5s) with room to spare or the row files as idle.
done     stops at `run`     -> v  green, once the idle window passes
blocked  stops, asks a y/n  -> o  red; checked before done, so it wins
idle     one line, too short a burst to count as work -> .  dim
`folder` files the row under one of the dock folders below, staged before
filming rather than during it: this clip is about what the badges say,
and a list reorganising itself is the other clip.
